01.r: The Levites are the ones who carry out the work of the sanctuary.
01.n: The verb carries the Hebrew 'and' that opens the verse, given here as the plain 'And'. The brief's lexicon lists 'to serve (with Levitical service)' among its senses. Verb and object share a root: literally 'serve the service'.

02.r: The tribe of Levi as a whole.
02.n: Singular in Hebrew; BDB: with the article, used as a collective. The translations make it plural.

03.r: Stresses that this work is the Levites' and no one else's.
03.n: The pronoun 'he' written out after the verb's subject, for emphasis. The JPS 'alone' and the DRC 'only' draw out that emphasis.

04.r: Marks 'the service' as the object of 'serve'.
04.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the service of'.

05.r: The work done at the sanctuary.
05.n: Gesenius: labour, work, and then work, business, office.

07.r: Where God meets with his people.
07.n: BDB: appointed time, place, meeting. The KJV and Geneva say 'the congregation'; the DRC leaves it out.

08.n: The pronoun is written out, for emphasis; the YLT shows it with 'they, they'.

09.r: They will carry the guilt that comes with work at the sanctuary.
09.n: The verb is 'lift, carry'; with 'iniquity' as its object it means to bear guilt or its penalty.

10.r: The guilt for any wrong done in approaching the sanctuary.
10.n: BDB: iniquity, guilt, or punishment of iniquity, not always easy to tell apart. Whose iniquity 'their' means (the Levites' own, or the people's) the Hebrew leaves open; the DRC reads 'the sins of the people'.

11.r: A fixed rule, not a passing arrangement.
11.n: Gesenius: that which is established or defined, spoken of a single law or ordinance.

12.r: The rule has no end date.
12.n: Literally 'a statute of perpetuity'. Gesenius: properly what is hidden, a long time whose end is not defined; eternity, perpetuity.

13.r: Binding on every generation to come.
13.n: Literally 'to your generations'. 'Your' is Israel, addressed through Aaron.

14.r: Within the tribes as the land is shared out.

s: they shall take as an inheritance
18.r: The Levites take no tribal land.
18.n: Gesenius: to receive any thing as a possession, very frequently used of Israel acquiring Canaan.

19.r: A tribal share of the land.
19.n: Verb and noun share a root: literally 'they shall not inherit an inheritance'. Gesenius notes the noun is often used of the territory assigned to each tribe.

01.n: λειτουργέω, to perform a public or sacred service.

05.n: λειτουργία, the service of the sanctuary. English 'liturgy' comes from it.

07.n: μαρτύριον, witness: the Greek calls it 'the tent of witness'.

09.n: λαμβάνω, take, receive: 'they shall take on their sins'.

10.n: ἁμάρτημα, sin, a wrong done, where the Hebrew word also covers guilt and its penalty.

13.n: The Greek says 'their generations' where the Hebrew has 'your'.
